title: Fleet Zipper: topology-aware graceful pool transition for zero-surge dedicated upgrades
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools between runtime versions currently causes transient capacity spikes and tenant-level SLA drift during naive drains. Existing drain strategies produce multi-tenant surges when autoscalers respond late or when KV cache repopulation increases per-token cost. We need a repeatable, topology-aware transition strategy that minimizes service surge, preserves latency SLOs, and composes cleanly with autoscaler handshakes and LTS channel pins.

Proposal (Fleet Zipper):
- Pairing model: create ephemeral donor/recipient "zipper" pairs inside a pool slice where nodes are topology-aware (same rack/az when possible) so network variance and cold cache effects are bounded.
- Lease-based autoscaler handshake: introduce a short-lived "drain lease" token acquired by the upgrade controller which signals intent to drain a node. Autoscaler acknowledges by pre-provisioning equivalent capacity or marking admission windows for affected tenants.
- Incremental zipper sweep: perform small micro-drains (1-3 nodes) across independent slices concurrently rather than bulk draining. Each zipper step waits for rollout gates before progressing.
- Rollout gates and metrics: require pass for: 1) 5m error budget remaining > 0.8, 2) 95th token latency regression < 10% vs baseline, 3) queue depth and backlog growth stable, 4) per-tenant request drop < 0.5%. Gates evaluated centrally via Console SLO dashboard endpoints.
- Topology-aware placement: when selecting recipient nodes prefer same-rack or same-toe to reduce cross-traffic; fallback to cross-az only when capacity hedges are in place.
- KV cache prewarming: use a warmup replay agent that replays most-recent prefixes for active tenants into recipient nodes pre-cutover. Warmup runs under a throttling budget to avoid causing traffic spikes.
- Tenant admission windows: critical/enterprise tenants may be islanded for isolated cutovers (configured via tenant tags). Non-islanded tenants use rolling admission windows with soft limits to avoid concentrated retries.
- Fallback and fast-rollback: traffic router configured with per-pool variant tags (runtime-1.21 LTS vs candidate). If a zipper step breaches gate thresholds, traffic is rolled back to prior variant for the affected slice and drain leases are returned.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Controller changes: implement zipper controller that manages pairing, drain leases, and gate evaluation (runtime-1.22 branch).
2) Autoscaler contract: add an API for drain_lease lifecycle (request, acknowledge, provisioned, release). Short protocol spec and e2e tests.
3) KV warmup service: lightweight replay worker + throttling. Metrics for warmup progress and induced load.
4) Console integration: per-step gate visualization and one-click pause/abort in runbook.
5) Rollout infra: router feature flags for per-slice variant routing and quick rollback.
6) Runbook & playbooks: step-by-step operator runbook, escalation paths, and PagerDuty play.

Gate criteria (concrete thresholds to start):
- Error budget: rolling 1h error rate must be within 75% of budget (configurable per-customer).
- Latency: P95 tokens latency regression <= 10% over baseline; P99 regression <= 20% for non-critical tenants.
- Capacity: autoscaler headroom must confirm +10% spare capacity for 5m after drain ack.
- Backlog: queue depth increase <= 5% vs baseline.
- KV cold-hit ratio: must stabilize below 15% after warmup for 10m.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New Console panels: zipper-step status, drain_lease table, warmup progress, per-tenant admission windows, pre/post latency/throughput deltas.
- Traces: annotate traces with zipper_step_id and drain_lease_id for root-cause analysis.
- Alerts: automated alert on gate breach (severity on customer_impact tag), plus an auto-pause action.

Safety & rollback:
- Automatic pause+rollback if any gate triggers major threshold breach for 2 consecutive zipper steps.
- Fast-rollback route toggles wired to a single CLI command and console button; rollback must not require node-level reboots.
- Postmortem cadence: mandatory post-release review within 72h for any step that triggered a pause.

Dependencies: autoscaler API changes, router variant routing support, console SLO endpoints, warmup worker prototype.

Why different from naive drains:
- Spreads eviction pressure across topology-aware slices instead of concentrated bulk evictions.
- Coordinates with autoscaler to avoid reactive scale-ups that amplify short-term demand.
- Prewarms caches to reduce cold-start latency and token cost spikes.

Deliverables (MVP):
- zipper controller + drain_lease API, autoscaler ack flow, and a basic warmup worker.
- Console gating UI and a small rollout runbook.
- Canary: single tenant islanded canary for runtime-1.22 in a single pool slice.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Can complete a zipper sweep on a small pool (<= 100 nodes) with no more than 3% SLO regressions across monitored tenants during canary.
- Autoscaler acknowledgements observed in 95% of lease requests in < 30s in staging.
- Warmup reduces KV cold-hit ratio by > 40% vs no-warmup baseline in controlled replay tests.

Longer-term: integrate with LTS channel mappings so customers can pin pool slices to specific LTS variants and use zipper controller for safe intra-LTS minor upgrades.
